entities.name: Languages
entities.summary: Language families and the languages descended from them. Placement here is by linguistic descent, not geography.

entities.name: Religions & Traditions
entities.summary: Religions, denominations, schools and legal traditions, filed by descent from what they grew out of.

entities.name: Trade & Exchange Networks
entities.summary: Systems of exchange that were neither states nor places, and that moved goods, people, faith and disease.

entities.name: Technological Thresholds
entities.summary: First attainments of a capability after the prehistoric record, each a lower bound that new evidence can only move older.

entities.name: Proto-Afroasiatic
entities.summary: Reconstructed ancestor of Semitic, Egyptian, Berber, Chadic and Cushitic; among the deepest families with a serious reconstruction.

entities.name: Proto-Semitic
entities.summary: Ancestor of Akkadian, Hebrew, Aramaic and Arabic, reconstructed largely from their shared triconsonantal roots.

entities.name: Akkadian
entities.summary: The first Semitic language written down, and the diplomatic language of the Bronze Age Near East.

entities.name: Aramaic
entities.summary: Administrative language of the Achaemenid Empire and still spoken by small communities today.

entities.name: Hebrew
entities.summary: Ceased to be a vernacular for roughly seventeen centuries and was revived as one, which almost no other language has managed.

entities.name: Arabic
entities.summary: Spread with Islam from a peninsular vernacular to the liturgical and literary language of much of Afro-Eurasia.

entities.name: Egyptian
entities.summary: Attested across four thousand years, from hieroglyphs to Coptic, the longest documented history of any language.

entities.name: Proto-Indo-European
entities.summary: Reconstructed ancestor of most languages of Europe and much of South Asia; its homeland is still argued.

entities.name: Proto-Indo-Iranian
entities.summary: The branch that carried Indo-European speech into Iran and South Asia.

entities.name: Sanskrit
entities.summary: Language of the Vedas, and the grammar Panini wrote for it is still the most complete description of any ancient language.

entities.name: Avestan
entities.summary: Language of the Zoroastrian liturgy, preserved orally for centuries before it was written.

entities.name: Hittite
entities.summary: The earliest attested Indo-European language, and its decipherment reshaped the whole reconstruction.

entities.name: Ancient Greek
entities.summary: Written first in Linear B, then in the alphabet that carried Homer, tragedy and Greek philosophy.

entities.name: Latin
entities.summary: Ancestor of the Romance languages and the learned language of western Europe long after it stopped being anyone's first.

entities.name: Proto-Uralic
entities.summary: Reconstructed ancestor of Finnish, Hungarian, Estonian and the Samoyedic languages of Siberia.

entities.name: Proto-Sino-Tibetan
entities.summary: Reconstructed ancestor of Chinese, Tibetan and Burmese; its internal structure is much less settled than Indo-European's.

entities.name: Old Chinese
entities.summary: The language of the oracle bones and the Confucian classics, reconstructed partly from rhymes in early poetry.

entities.name: Proto-Austronesian
entities.summary: Ancestor of a family that spread from Taiwan across the Pacific to Madagascar, the widest pre-modern dispersal of any.

entities.name: Proto-Bantu
entities.summary: Ancestor of some five hundred languages across sub-Saharan Africa, spread by the Bantu expansion.

entities.name: Proto-Dravidian
entities.summary: Reconstructed ancestor of Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam; possibly the language family of the Indus cities.

entities.name: Proto-Japonic
entities.summary: Ancestor of Japanese and the Ryukyuan languages, probably carried to the islands with wet-rice farming.

entities.name: Proto-Koreanic
entities.summary: Ancestor of Korean, whose relationship to Japonic remains one of the open questions of Asian linguistics.

entities.name: Sumerian
entities.summary: The first written language, and an isolate: no relative has ever been established for it.

entities.name: Elamite
entities.summary: Written beside Sumerian and Akkadian for two millennia and, like Sumerian, without known relatives.

entities.name: Etruscan
entities.summary: Non-Indo-European language of pre-Roman Italy, readable in script but still largely not understood.

entities.name: Classical Maya
entities.summary: The only pre-Columbian American writing system fully deciphered, recording dynastic history in its own words.

entities.name: Quechua
entities.summary: Spread as the administrative language of the Inca state and still spoken by millions across the Andes.

entities.name: Nahuatl
entities.summary: Language of the Aztec state, and the source of chocolate, tomato, avocado and coyote.

entities.name: Zoroastrianism
entities.summary: Persian tradition whose ideas about judgement, a final reckoning and cosmic dualism reached Judaism, Christianity and Islam.

entities.name: Judaism
entities.summary: Took its lasting shape around exile and return, and around a text rather than a temple.

entities.name: Hinduism
entities.summary: Less a single founding than a continuity of Vedic ritual, Upanishadic philosophy and devotional practice.

entities.name: Jainism
entities.summary: Holds non-violence as the first principle, extended to every living thing.

entities.name: Buddhism
entities.summary: Began as a teaching about the causes of suffering and became the first tradition to spread across Asia by persuasion.

entities.name: Theravada Buddhism
entities.summary: The school that kept the Pali canon, dominant across Sri Lanka and mainland Southeast Asia.

entities.name: Mahayana Buddhism
entities.summary: Shifted the goal from personal liberation to universal awakening, and carried Buddhism to China, Korea and Japan.

entities.name: Vajrayana Buddhism
entities.summary: Tantric Buddhism, transmitted into Tibet and the Himalaya.

entities.name: Confucianism
entities.summary: A tradition about conduct, family and government rather than gods, and the framework of Chinese administration for two millennia.

entities.name: Daoism
entities.summary: Philosophy and later religion built on acting with the grain of things rather than against it.

entities.name: Shinto
entities.summary: Japanese practice centred on kami and place, defined as a distinct religion largely in response to Buddhism.

entities.name: Christianity
entities.summary: Began as a movement within Judaism and became the state religion of the empire that had executed its founder.

entities.name: Islam
entities.summary: Began at Mecca and Medina and within a century governed from Iberia to the Indus.

entities.name: The Sunni-Shia Split
entities.summary: A dispute over succession to Muhammad that hardened into the enduring division of the Muslim world.

entities.name: Sufism
entities.summary: The mystical current of Islam, and the form in which it most often spread through South Asia and West Africa.

entities.name: The Great Schism
entities.summary: Formal separation of the Latin and Greek churches, after centuries of drift over authority and doctrine.

entities.name: Sikhism
entities.summary: Founded by Nanak in Punjab, rejecting caste and ritual in favour of one God and honest work.

entities.name: Manichaeism
entities.summary: A deliberately universal religion that reached from Rome to China and then was extinguished almost everywhere.

entities.name: Sarmatians
entities.summary: Successors to the Scythians on the western steppe, and heavy cavalry the Romans learned from.

entities.name: Xiongnu
entities.summary: Steppe confederation whose pressure shaped Han policy, the frontier walls, and the westward movement of peoples.

entities.name: Huns
entities.summary: Arrived on the Danube within a generation and broke the Roman order in the west without ever holding a city.

entities.name: Turkic Peoples
entities.summary: Spread from Mongolia to Anatolia over a millennium, founding states from the Gokturks to the Ottomans.

entities.name: Sea Peoples
entities.summary: Raiders named in Egyptian inscriptions, associated with the collapse of the Bronze Age eastern Mediterranean.

entities.name: Celtic Peoples
entities.summary: A shared language, art and metalwork across Iron Age Europe, never a single state.

entities.name: Germanic Peoples
entities.summary: Named as an outside threat by Rome and eventually the founders of its successor kingdoms.

entities.name: Slavic Peoples
entities.summary: Expanded across eastern and southeastern Europe in the centuries after Rome, with little written trace of the process.

entities.name: Sami
entities.summary: Reindeer-herding people of Fennoscandia, and among the few European peoples never to form a state.

entities.name: Bantu-Speaking Peoples
entities.summary: Their expansion carried farming, ironworking and a language family across a third of a continent.

entities.name: Amazigh
entities.summary: Indigenous peoples of North Africa, continuous through Punic, Roman, Arab and French rule.

entities.name: Thule
entities.summary: Ancestors of the Inuit, who crossed the American Arctic in a few centuries with dog sleds and toggling harpoons.

entities.name: Aboriginal Australians
entities.summary: The longest continuous cultural tradition known, with oral accounts that appear to record post-glacial sea-level rise.

entities.name: The Silk Road
entities.summary: Not one road but a relay of routes moving silk, horses, faith and plague between China, India, Persia and Rome.

entities.name: Indian Ocean Trade
entities.summary: Monsoon-driven and older than the Silk Road, carrying more goods by volume than any overland route.

entities.name: Trans-Saharan Trade
entities.summary: Gold north, salt south, and the wealth that built Mali, Songhai and the libraries of Timbuktu.

entities.name: The Amber Road
entities.summary: Baltic amber reaching the Mediterranean, and evidence of long-distance exchange well before any empire organised it.

entities.name: The Hanseatic League
entities.summary: A league of merchant towns that ran the northern European economy without being a state.

entities.name: The Atlantic Slave Trade
entities.summary: Some twelve million people shipped from Africa to the Americas, and the demographic and economic foundation of the Atlantic world.

entities.name: The Manila Galleon Trade
entities.summary: Silver from Mexico for Chinese silk and porcelain, and the first sustained commercial link across the Pacific.

entities.name: Confucius
entities.summary: Taught that government rests on the character of those who govern; had no office of consequence and shaped a civilisation.

entities.name: Laozi
entities.summary: Traditional author of the Daodejing, and possibly a composite of several figures.

entities.name: Siddhartha Gautama
entities.summary: Left a princely household to answer why there is suffering, and founded the tradition that became Buddhism.

entities.name: Mahavira
entities.summary: Contemporary of the Buddha and the figure Jainism takes its historical shape from.

entities.name: Zoroaster
entities.summary: Prophet of the first tradition to frame history as a moral struggle with an end.

entities.name: Socrates
entities.summary: Wrote nothing, was executed by his own city, and set the shape of philosophical argument since.

entities.name: Aristotle
entities.summary: Attempted a systematic account of everything, and his errors held authority nearly as long as his insights.

entities.name: Archimedes
entities.summary: Came nearer to calculus than anyone would for eighteen centuries.

entities.name: Al-Khwarizmi
entities.summary: His name became algorithm and his book's title became algebra.

entities.name: Ibn Sina
entities.summary: His medical canon was the standard text in Europe and the Islamic world for six hundred years.

entities.name: Aryabhata
entities.summary: Gave a place-value system, an accurate value for pi, and a rotating Earth.

entities.name: Johannes Gutenberg
entities.summary: Combined movable type, oil ink and the press into something that made copying cheap enough to change what could be thought.

entities.name: Iron Smelting
entities.summary: Hittite-era bloomery iron; the metal that made tools cheap rather than precious.

entities.name: Alphabetic Writing
entities.summary: One sign per sound rather than per syllable or word, which made literacy learnable in weeks.

entities.name: Zero as a Number
entities.summary: Brahmagupta gave rules for arithmetic with zero and with negatives, not merely a placeholder.

entities.name: Papermaking
entities.summary: Cheap writing material from plant fibre, in China centuries before it reached the west.

entities.name: Woodblock Printing
entities.summary: Text carved and reproduced in quantity in Tang China, long before movable type.

entities.name: Movable Type
entities.summary: Bi Sheng's ceramic type; reusable characters four centuries before Gutenberg.

entities.name: Gunpowder
entities.summary: A Chinese alchemical accident that ended the military logic of the walled city.

entities.name: Magnetic Compass
entities.summary: Made open-water navigation repeatable rather than lucky.

entities.name: The Printing Press
entities.summary: Movable metal type and a screw press in Mainz; the first information technology with a mass market.

entities.name: The Telescope
entities.summary: Turned the sky into something to be examined rather than contemplated.

entities.name: The Steam Engine
entities.summary: Newcomen's atmospheric engine; work no longer limited by muscle, wind or falling water.

entities.name: Vaccination
entities.summary: Jenner's cowpox inoculation, and the beginning of deliberate control of infectious disease.

entities.name: Germ Theory of Disease
entities.summary: Established that specific microbes cause specific diseases, which made surgery survivable.

entities.name: Practical Electric Lighting
entities.summary: Decoupled the working day from daylight.

entities.name: Powered Flight
entities.summary: Twelve seconds at Kitty Hawk.

entities.name: Antibiotics
entities.summary: Fleming's penicillin; bacterial infection stopped being a common cause of death.

entities.name: Controlled Nuclear Fission
entities.summary: The first self-sustaining chain reaction, under a squash court in Chicago.

entities.name: The Transistor
entities.summary: The switch that made computing small, cheap and eventually universal.

entities.name: The Integrated Circuit
entities.summary: Many components on one wafer, which is why computing kept getting cheaper.

entities.name: Packet-Switched Networking
entities.summary: The first ARPANET link; messages broken into pieces that route themselves.

entities.name: The Human Genome Sequenced
entities.summary: A species reading its own instructions.
